title: Letters notes.json, format 1
description: The notes on a document: comments, import notes and conflicts, each anchored to a passage. A reader keeps the fields and note types it does not know and writes them back. Note ids are unique, which this schema cannot express.

format.description: Rises only for a breaking change.

type.description: comment, import or conflict. A note of any other type is kept as written.

content.description: What the note says, in the same runs as document text.

versions.description: The two versions of the anchored block, the later edit last: the one document.json shows until one is picked. Picking one resolves the note.

anchor.description: The passage a note sits on: a whole block, or a range of its text in UTF-8 bytes with start no greater than end.

block.description: The id of a block in document.json.

stood.description: Where the block stood, for a note on a block that document.json no longer holds, as a conflict whose later side took the block away. With neither field it stood first in the document.

after.description: The id of the nearest block before it in the same parent that was still there.

parent.description: The id of the block that held it. Absent at the top level.

version.description: One side of a conflict. A side with no block took the block away, and its author and time say who did and when.

author.description: Who last changed this side. Empty when that writer gave no name.

stable.description: One end of the range as a position in the document's history, which Letters uses to keep the anchor on its text through edits and merges. Other tools keep it as written, and drop both when they change the range.

author.description: The name shown beside the note.
